chunks: Al-Husayn ibn Sa'id from Fadalah from Jamil ibn Darraj from Aban from Abd al-Rahman ibn Abi Uqbah from Humran from one of the Imams (peace be upon them) said:
"My father would pray upon the leather prayer mat, placing it on the ground, and prostrate upon it. If there was no leather mat, he would place a stone on the ground where he would prostrate."
ai.seo_question: What did the Imams use for prayer mats and prostration surfaces?
ai.summary: This hadith, transmitted through the chain of Aban ibn Taghlib, clarifies the juristic principle that prostration (sujood) must occur on a natural, pure surface, validating the use of a leather mat (khumrah) or, in its absence, a stone placed on the ground. It underscores the Shia emphasis on the physical purity and natural origin of prayer surfaces, ensuring that the forehead touches something distinct from the earth itself to maintain ritual validity.
